title: Coordinate-face base change for an unpunctured full root tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ use all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart, and $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ a reduced strict normal crossings boundary whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale and put
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\leq d\leq r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right).$$
The index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility, with transition $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a profinite set $P$ let $T[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_a}\coprod_{P_a}T$, and let $\mathcal N_P$ be the pullback of $\mathcal N$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].
Write $q_P:T[P]\to U$ for the structural map. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(t_j)_{j\in J})$, with closed inclusion $g_J:U_J\hookrightarrow U$, and put
$$T_J=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}(R/(t_j)_{j\in J})[x_{d,n}]_{d\notin J}/(x_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)_{d\notin J}\right).$$
Let $e_J:T_J\to T$ set all roots indexed by $J$ to zero; let $q_{J,P}:T_J[P]\to U_J$ be structural and $e_{J,P}:T_J[P]\to T[P]$ the induced map. Use closed inverse/direct-image adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Define $\beta_{J,P}$ to be the adjunct of
$$q_P^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\longrightarrow\mathcal N_P[0]$$
after pulling the counit back by $e_{J,P}$ and identifying $q_{J,P}^*g_J^*=e_{J,P}^*q_P^*$. Then
$$\beta_{J,P}:g_J^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R(q_{J,P})_*e_{J,P}^*\mathcal N_P[0]$$
is an isomorphism. Equivalently it is the usual cartesian exchange followed by restriction from $T\times_UU_J$ to $T_J$; the latter map is the surjective closed immersion killing all the nilpotent roots indexed by $J$. The adjunct back on $U$ is exactly $Rq_{P,*}$ of the closed unit for $e_{J,P}$, with the canonical composition identification. The comparisons agree for $J\subseteq J'$ with successive coordinate restriction and are compatible with restriction to open subsets of $U$. They are natural in $P$, in maps of the supplied lisse modules, and under pro-etale base change of $U$, and commute with root-tower automorphisms preserving these faces and with the supplied module actions. For a profinite family indexed by $Q$, compatibility is equality on the $Q$-parametrized terms. The cases $J=\varnothing$, $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, rank zero and empty charts are included. There is no puncture, outer/inner partition, or closed union in this assertion.

proof.text: The parameter-root lemma gives $q_P$ integral. Put $A=\varinjlim_nR[x_{d,n}]_{d\notin J}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)$, with the given transitions. Apply that lemma again over $A$ to the parameters $t_j$, $j\in J$: its full root algebra is $S$ by the presentations: maps fixing all root generators are mutually inverse, and its zero-root quotient is the algebra of $T_J$. Thus $a:T_J[P]\hookrightarrow B_J=T[P]\times_UU_J$ is surjective closed with nil kernel. These identifications commute with the stated base and parameter maps. Also $e_{J,P}$ has complement $\bigcup_{j\in J}D(t_j)$: the root equations make vanishing of $t_j$ equivalent to vanishing of all its roots.

proof.text: Write $h:B_J\to T[P]$ and $f:B_J\to U_J$. Pullback preserves finite free trivializations, so $\mathcal N_P$ is lisse. Integral-lisse closed base change applies to $q_P,g_J,C_F$, giving $g_J^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\simeq Rf_*h^*\mathcal N_P[0]$. Surjective-closed condensed pullback for $a$ is an exact equivalence; its unit gives the further isomorphism to $R(fa)_*a^*h^*\mathcal N_P[0]$.

proof.text: The composite has transpose $e_{J,P}^*\varepsilon_{q_P}$, hence is precisely $\beta_{J,P}$. Transposing along $g_J$ instead gives $Rq_{P,*}(\eta_{e_{J,P}})$: its further $q_P$-transpose is the same pulled-back counit. Derived composition normalization identifies these units and counits. For $J\subseteq J'$, quotienting first by the $J$-roots and then by the remaining $J'$-roots kills exactly the $J'$-roots; mate pasting proves successive restriction compatibility.

proof.text: Integral-lisse exchange supplies pro-etale base-change naturality of the cartesian part, including open restriction and $U[Q]$. For the face unit, localized sites and derived sections identify the complexes on a test $V\to U'$ as $I(T[P]\times_U V)$; internal-module transport preserves their counits. Thus the same pulled-back-counit transpose proves face naturality. Maps of $P$, module maps and face-preserving automorphisms commute with this counit and the quotient maps. For a $Q$-family take these equations on $T[P][Q]=T[P\times Q]$ itself; transposition gives the action compatibility there.

proof.text: For empty $J$, the quotient is the identity and the triangle identity gives the identity comparison. Full $J$ leaves no root variables; $r=0$ has only empty $J$. Rank zero, empty $P$ and empty charts give zero complexes. The nil ideal requires no uniform exponent.

Its zero-root quotient is the algebra of T_J, its B_P is T[P]⊗_R R/(t_J) = B_J, and i = e_J. So a is a surjective closed immersion with nil kernel and ha = e. The condensed surjective-closed equivalence for a makes a_* exact, so the derived unit is invertible, and derived composition gives R(fa)_* with fa = q_{J,P}. Step 3: the triangle identity gives transpose e^*ε, so the composite is β; the g_J-side transpose is Rq_*η_e; J⊆J′ follows by mate pasting. Steps 4–5 keep the old steps 8–9: localized K-injective sections I(T[P]×_U V), transport of the counit, naturality in P, in modules, under automorphisms and on T[P×Q]. The edge cases J empty or all, r=0, P empty, rank 0 and a unit t_j check out. The note asked for at least 2 new nodes and the delivery has 0.
